data.name: Ashoke
data.gender_notes: Ashoke is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words ‘as’ meaning ‘immeasurable’ and ‘shoka’ meaning ‘sorrow’. The name Ashoke is bestowed upon a child to represent the idea that even in the face of great sorrow, one remains immortal and invincible. The name Ashoke carries the meaning “Immortal, Invincible” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ashoke usually hope their child will grow to embody immortal, invincible and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace the strength and resilience within to overcome adversity.
data.etymology: Ashoke belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Immortal, Invincible.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashoke total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ashoke has its roots in the rich cultural heritage of Hinduism, where it holds a unique significance in naming a child. The name embodies values of resilience, strength and endurance in the face of adversity. It reminds us of the famous tale of Lord Shiva, who wears the mark of Ashoka (the first Letter of his name) on his forehead to symbolize his eternal wandering in search of his consort, Sati, who had immolated herself in the sacrificial pyre.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Ashoke represents the indomitable spirit within an individual that remains immutable even in the most sorrowful times. The name imparts a deep sense of hope, strength and fortitude, encouraging the bearer to endure hardships and bounce back stronger. It serves as a reminder that no matter how deep or profound our grief, we remain capable of rising above it and continuing our journey through life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ashoke: Radiant as the sun, infusing hope and courage, symbolizing the indomitable spirit that shines through challenges in life.

historical_references.reference: Ashoka the Great was a Mauryan emperor who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent from 268 to 232 BC.
Ashoka is best known for his rock edicts and pillars, which were inscribed with directions for the moral and social conduct of his people.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Ashoke gains modern recognition in various spheres, including technology, business, and philanthropy. In the tech industry, Ashoke Chakravarty, an entrepreneur and CEO of Cognitivescale, is a notable figure. His company specializes in AI and machine learning solutions. In the business realm, Ashoke Ghosh, a renowned financial analyst and author, frequently appears in financial news and publications, such as Forbes. Lastly, Ashoke Nanda, a prominent philanthropist, is active in charitable foundations and organizations. His foundation, the Ashok Nanda Foundation, focuses on education and community development.
